title: Idgham and heavy letters in Ash-Shams: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y4 lesson 16 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Idgham and heavy letters in Ash-Shams rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 16. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Two rules at once
points: Look ahead to the next letter

panels.title: Peer check: kind correction
points: Point to one word to fix

keywords.def: merging a noon sakinah or tanween into the next letter

questions.q: Recite 91:5 to 7 and name every rule you use.
questions.a: 91:6 ط heavy (طَحَىٰهَا); 91:7 idgham with ghunnah (نَفْسٍۢ وَمَا).

questions.q: How many counts is a ghunnah?
In breakout pairs, recite 91:1 to 8 to each other; the listener ticks heavy letters and idgham on the pupil PDF. Today's rota group recites to the teacher.
questions.a: Each pupil recites; the partner's sheet shows ticks for ض ق ط and the idgham in 91:7.

questions.q: Extend: find one idgham in Al-Layl.
Stretch: find an ikhfa in Ash-Shams 91:9 to 10 (next lesson's ayat).
Which word has a heavy letter AND is in Ash-Shams?
questions.a: A) طَحَىٰهَا. طَحَىٰهَا starts with ط, a heavy letter. تَلَىٰهَا and بَنَىٰهَا have only light letters.

questions.q: Think again: A good recitation uses many rules at once, like a cyclist steering, pedalling and looking ahead. Which rule do you find hardest to remember?
questions.a: Many say the hum of idgham or keeping heavy letters full; practice makes it automatic.
